---
title: "Build a PTI"
description: >
  Overview of the pipeline that takes raw country data through to a
  deployed Project Targeting Index (PTI) Shiny dashboard with
  `devPTIpack`.
---

A **Project Targeting Index (PTI)** is a composite map ranking
sub-national administrative units against a set of weighted indicators —
useful for guiding the spatial allocation of programs and investments.
`devPTIpack` is the toolkit that turns your country's boundaries
(shapes) + indicators (data) into a deployed Shiny dashboard.

This page is the **journey map**. Each step is a focused tutorial; this
overview tells you which one to read when, and how the pieces fit
together. Pair it with [PTI Methodology](methodology.html) (the
conceptual *why*) and [Data preparation reference](dataprep.html) (the
canonical column-by-column *what*).

## What data does a PTI app need?

Two inputs are mandatory; one is optional:

| Input | Format | Step that produces it |
|------------------|----------------------------|---------------------------|
| Boundary shapes | Named list of `sf` tibbles, one per admin level. | [Step 1](build-pti-1-shapefiles.html) |
| User data + metadata | Multi-sheet `.xlsx` — indicator dictionary plus per-admin values. | [Step 3](build-pti-3-metadata.html) |
| HEX gridded data | H3 hex-grid indicator values pulled from World Bank Space2Stats. *Optional.* | [Step 4](build-pti-4-hex.html) |

The full column contract for both lives in [Data preparation
reference](dataprep.html).

## Reproducible quick start — the bundled Rwanda app

The fastest way to see a working PTI app is the Rwanda template that
ships with the package:

``` r
#| eval: false
install.packages("pak"); pak::pak("worldbank/devPTIpack")
library(devPTIpack)
create_new_pti("~/projects/rwa_pti")   # scaffold the project
setwd("~/projects/rwa_pti")            # run from the project root
source("00-master.R")                  # run the whole pipeline
shiny::runApp("app.R")                 # preview the app locally
```

Five Rwandan provinces, 30 districts, three synthetic indicators, two
pillars — a complete dashboard, plus a `docs/` data-quality website, in
a few minutes. Once that runs, swap in your country's data and re-run
the same pipeline.

## The journey

The pipeline is seven tutorials (Steps 0–6). Steps 1–5 write the files
the deployed app reads into `app-data/`, and render a `docs/`
data-quality website you can review locally or publish.

| \# | Step | What it does | Required? |
|-----|-----------|-----------------------------|---------------|
| 0 | [Setup](build-pti-0-setup.html) | Install `devPTIpack`, scaffold the project folder via `create_new_pti()`. | Always |
| 1 | [Shapefiles](build-pti-1-shapefiles.html) | Load + validate administrative boundaries, build the hex grid, save `app-data/shapes.rds`. | Always |
| 2 | [Zonal stats](build-pti-2-zonal-stats.html) | Extract polygon-level indicators from raster surfaces into `sample-data/`. | Optional |
| 3 | [User data](build-pti-3-metadata.html) | Merge your indicator values into the metadata workbook; validate against shapes; save `app-data/metadata-user.xlsx`. | Always |
| 4 | [HEX data](build-pti-4-hex.html) | Pull H3 hex-grid indicators from World Bank Space2Stats; save `app-data/metadata-hex.xlsx`. | Optional |
| 5 | [Compile & finalise](build-pti-5-compile.html) | Merge all metadata + re-validate + render the data-quality report + zip GeoJSONs. | Always |
| 6 | [Deploy](build-pti-6-deploy.html) | Publish the app to Posit Connect / shinyapps.io, and the `docs/` website to GitHub Pages. | When sharing |

**Step 4 is order-flexible** — it produces an independent
`app-data/metadata-hex.xlsx` that Step 5 merges with the user metadata.
You can run it before or after Step 3. The other steps run sequentially.

## The `00-master.R` shortcut

Each scaffolded project ships
[`00-master.R`](https://github.com/worldbank/devPTIpack/blob/main/inst/template_pti/00-master.R)
— a pipeline orchestrator that calls `quarto::quarto_render()` on the
step `.qmd` files top-to-bottom, populates `app-data/`, renders the
data-quality report, and builds the `docs/` website. After your first
walkthrough, **`source("00-master.R")` is the everyday command** — it
re-runs the whole pipeline every time your raw inputs change. Comment /
uncomment lines to skip optional steps (Step 2 is off by default) or
pause work.

The website tutorials (this page and Steps 0–6) are how you *learn* the
pipeline. `00-master.R` is how you *operate* it once you know it.

## Where to start

- **First time?** Begin with [Step 0 — Setup](build-pti-0-setup.html)
  and follow the steps top to bottom.
- **Already familiar with `devPTIpack`?** Jump straight to the step
  you're working on. Each tutorial has a "Next" pointer back into the
  chain.
- **Reference question** ("what columns does the metadata sheet need?")
  — go to [Data preparation reference](dataprep.html).
- **Method question** ("how is the PTI score computed?") — go to [PTI
  Methodology](methodology.html).
